title: Dependencies Installation and Project Structure Initialization
description: Set up the development environment for the DualRayRank solver-in-the-loop repair experiments. The project requires: (1) vLLM for efficient LLM inference with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, (2) highspy (HiGHS Python bindings) for LP/MIP solving, IIS computation, and dual ray extraction, (3) standard data processing and visualization libraries. The codebase will be organized to support the full pipeline: natural-language-to-LP generation, solver-based verification, infeasibility diagnosis (IIS and dual ray), prompt construction for three feedback conditions (IIS-TopK, DualRay-TopK, DualRay-TopK+Weights), and repair evaluation.
summary: Environment configured: .venv with Python 3.12.12, torch 2.9.1+cu129, vllm 0.12.1, highspy 1.13.1, transformers, datasets, numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, seaborn, tqdm, jsonlines. Project structure created under dualrayrank/ with data/solver/prompts/inference/evaluation/analysis/scripts/outputs/results modules. MAMO benchmark cloned (652 EasyLP + 211 ComplexLP). Implemented load_mamo.py, lp_parser.py, and highs_wrapper.py with solve/IIS/dual-ray extraction. Key note: HiGHS IIS requires iis_strategy>=2.

title: Attempt-0 Generation (No Repair) on MAMO
description:
Generate LP models from natural-language optimization problems using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with greedy decoding (temperature=0) and evaluate pass@1 on MAMO-Optimization (EasyLP + ComplexLP). This establishes the base performance without any repair, providing the attempt-0 results and identifying the infeasible subset that all repair methods will operate on.

Reference: "Mamo: a Mathematical Modeling Benchmark with Solvers" | https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/Mamo
summary: Ran experiment: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct greedy (temp=0) on 863 MAMO instances. Overall pass@1=58.05% (501/863), EasyLP=71.17% (464/652), ComplexLP=17.54% (37/211). Infeasible rate=3.59% (31 instances: 9 EasyLP + 22 ComplexLP). Status distribution: pass=501, fail-wrong-objective=269, fail-error=54, fail-infeasible=31, fail-unbounded=8. Infeasible instance list saved for downstream repair experiments. Files: {difficulty}_{id}.lp naming convention.

title: Best-of-2 Inference Scaling Control on MAMO
description:
Evaluate a compute-matched inference-time scaling baseline: generate two stochastic samples (temperature=0.7, top_p=0.95) for each MAMO instance and select the first solver-correct one. This controls for the possibility that a second inference call alone (without any solver diagnostic feedback) could improve pass@1, ensuring that any gains from repair methods are attributable to the feedback content rather than simply having a second chance.

Reference: "Mamo: a Mathematical Modeling Benchmark with Solvers" | https://github.com/FreedomIntelligence/Mamo
summary: Best-of-2 stochastic sampling (temp=0.7, top_p=0.95, n=2) with oracle selection across 3 seeds [42,123,456]. Overall pass@1: 65.12%+/-0.66% (vs 58.05% greedy attempt-0, +7.07pp). EasyLP: 79.50%+/-0.51% (+8.33pp). ComplexLP: 20.70%+/-1.56% (+3.16pp). This sets the bar for repair methods: they must exceed 65.12% to demonstrate solver feedback adds value beyond a second generation attempt.

title: IIS-TopK Repair (Condition A) on MAMO
description:
Evaluate the IIS-TopK repair baseline on the infeasible subset from attempt-0. For each infeasible instance, compute the IIS on the LP relaxation using HiGHS, sort IIS constraints by constraint name (deterministic ordering), truncate to the top K=5 constraints, and provide these as feedback in a repair prompt. The LLM generates a corrected `.lp` file in one repair attempt. This is the primary baseline against which the proposed DualRayRank methods are compared.

Reference: "Solver-in-the-Loop MDP-Based Benchmarks for Self-Correction and Behavioral Rationality in Operations Research" | https://github.com/CardinalOperations/or-debug-bench (IIS-based feedback approach)
summary: IIS-TopK repair baseline (Condition A, K=5) evaluated on 31 infeasible instances. Repair success rate: 1/31 (3.23%). Pass@1 after <=2 attempts: 58.17% overall (+0.12pp vs attempt-0). Only 1 EasyLP instance repaired; 0 ComplexLP. 16/31 instances had IIS>5 (truncation regime).

title: DualRay-TopK Repair (Condition B) on MAMO
description:
Implement and evaluate the proposed DualRayRank method (Condition B: names only, no weights) on the infeasible subset from attempt-0. For each infeasible instance, extract the Farkas dual ray (infeasibility certificate) from the LP relaxation using HiGHS, rank constraints by absolute multiplier magnitude |y_i|, select the top K=5 constraints, and provide these as feedback in a repair prompt without including the numeric multipliers. This tests whether the dual-ray-based constraint ranking/selection alone improves repair over the unranked IIS-TopK baseline. The key novelty is using solver-produced Farkas multipliers as a principled ranking signal for LLM-based optimization model repair.

Reference codebase: Builds upon the solver wrapper (`solver/highs_wrapper.py`) and repair prompt infrastructure (`prompts/repair_prompt.py`) implemented in previous items. HiGHS dual ray API: `h.getDualRay()` returns a vector of Farkas multipliers over constraint rows.
summary: Implemented DualRay-TopK feedback (Condition B) with Farkas dual ray ranking and evaluated on 31 infeasible instances. All 31 instances produced valid dual rays (no IIS fallback needed). Repair success: 1/31 (3.23%), same as IIS-TopK. Pass@1 after <=2 attempts: 502/863 (58.17%). Truncation regime (IIS>5): 0/16 repairs. Constraint ranking alone without numeric weights does not improve over unranked IIS-TopK.

title: Optimize: DualRay-TopK Repair (Condition B) on MAMO

title: DualRay-TopK+Weights Repair (Condition C) on MAMO
description:
Implement and evaluate the DualRayRank method with normalized weights (Condition C) on the infeasible subset from attempt-0. This extends Condition B by including normalized weight values w_i = |y_i| / sum_{j in TopK} |y_j| alongside the constraint text. This ablation tests whether providing the numeric magnitude information adds value beyond the constraint ranking/selection, addressing the question of whether LLMs can leverage quantitative infeasibility contribution signals.

Reference codebase: Builds upon the DualRay-TopK feedback module (`prompts/dualray_feedback.py`) and shared repair infrastructure from previous items.
summary: DualRay-TopK+Weights (Condition C, K=5, greedy) achieves 1/31 (3.23%) repair success rate, identical to Conditions A (IIS-TopK) and B (DualRay-TopK). Same single instance repaired (EasyLP_425). Adding normalized weights w_i = |y_i|/sum does not improve repair in greedy K=5 setting. All 31 instances used dual ray feedback. Truncation regime: 0/16. Results confirm that quantitative multiplier information alone does not help the LLM in single-attempt greedy mode -- benefit only appears with increased K and sampling diversity (C+ optimized: 3/31).

title: DualRayRank Effectiveness Evaluation
description: Evaluate whether the proposed DualRayRank method (dual-ray-based constraint ranking for LLM repair feedback) is effective compared to IIS-TopK and other baselines. The evaluation follows the decision rule defined in the research hypothesis: the primary comparison is between DualRay-TopK (Condition B) and IIS-TopK (Condition A) on the truncation regime (infeasible instances where IIS size > K=5). Secondary comparisons include DualRay-TopK+Weights (Condition C) vs Condition B, and all repair methods vs the Best-of-2 inference scaling control. Metrics: repair success rate on the infeasible subset, repair success rate on the truncation regime subset, and end-to-end Pass@1 after ≤2 attempts.
summary: Verdict: bad. The DualRayRank method does not outperform IIS-TopK under controlled comparison. On the truncation regime (IIS > K=5), both achieve 0/16 repair rate. Under controlled conditions (7B, K=5, greedy), B=A=C=1/31, same instance repaired (EasyLP_425). Truncation regime has only 16 instances (<50 gate, practical relevance refuted). Best-of-2 (65.12%) dominates all repair methods (max 58.86%) by ~6pp. Optimized 72B variant achieves 7/31 but is confounded with model capacity; only 1/16 truncation regime instance repaired. Primary hypothesis refuted; repair paradigm dominated by inference scaling.

title: IIS Size Distribution and Truncation Regime Analysis
description: Analyze the distribution of IIS sizes across the infeasible subset to characterize how often truncation (IIS size > K) occurs, which is the regime where dual-ray ranking is hypothesized to help. This analysis provides the critical context for interpreting the main results: if most IIS sets are small (≤K=5), the ranking advantage is moot; if many are large, the truncation bottleneck is real and ranking matters. Also analyze how IIS size varies by difficulty level (EasyLP vs ComplexLP).

title: Constraint Set Overlap Analysis (IIS-TopK vs DualRay-TopK)
description: Analyze the overlap between the constraint sets selected by IIS-TopK (Condition A) and DualRay-TopK (Condition B) for each infeasible instance. This diagnostic reveals whether the two feedback methods tend to select the same constraints (in which case the ranking advantage is purely about ordering) or different constraints (in which case the dual-ray signal identifies a different, potentially better, set of culprit constraints).

title: Dual Ray Validity and Numerical Stability Analysis
description: Analyze the reliability of Farkas dual ray extraction from HiGHS across the infeasible subset. This addresses a key risk factor identified in the hypothesis: dual rays may be numerically unstable or diffuse, producing a noisy ranking signal. The analysis examines: (a) how often dual ray extraction succeeds, (b) the sparsity and concentration of the multiplier vector, and (c) whether dual ray quality correlates with repair success.

title: Qualitative Case Study of Repair Outputs
description: Provide qualitative case studies comparing the repair outputs under IIS-TopK (A) and DualRay-TopK (B) feedback to illustrate concrete differences in how the LLM uses different feedback signals. Select representative instances from both success and failure cases in the truncation regime to provide interpretable examples for the paper.
